A1.evidence: The objective states that students will 'define AI literacy in their own words' and 'identify at least three distinct, industry-spanning AI use cases', which are measurable outcomes. The success criteria for the assessment task also provide clear expectations.

A2.evidence: The lesson plan includes a mix of learning activities (think-pair-share, mini-poll prompts, working definition, core components) and assessments (quick check, rubric). The activities are aligned with the outcomes, but there is no explicit mapping between the TLAs and assessment tasks.

A3.evidence: The lesson plan has a coherent sequence of learning activities (activate prior knowledge → model → guided → independent), but the timings are not realistic, and there is no clear indication of small steps or worked examples.

B1.evidence: The lesson plan includes a mix of Constructive/Interactive modes (think-pair-share, mini-poll prompts) and Passive/Active activities (slides, one-page scenarios). However, the time allocated to each activity is not specified.

B2.evidence: The lesson plan includes generative tasks (Use-Case Canvas) that require students to explain and justify their answers. The rubric for the assessment task also expects new ideas and links, not copies.

B3.evidence: The lesson plan includes some all-student response routines (mini-poll prompts) but lacks structured group work with roles and joint products. The instructor support is limited to circulating and probing for metrics, risks, and governance.

C1.evidence: The lesson plan includes one substantial retrieval (quick check) but lacks high-effort formats (free recall, short-answer). The assessment task also has a mix of low- and high-effort questions.

C2.evidence: The lesson plan includes aligned exit tickets/mini-quizzes/oral checks with immediate use (instructor support, circulation) and task-focused feedback time. However, the feedback plan is not explicitly stated.

C3.evidence: The lesson plan lacks in-lesson spacing between retrievals and planned delayed cumulative checks (≈2 days & 1 week). The assessment task also does not include prior content.

D1.evidence: The lesson plan includes full worked examples (core components) and a timed, scaffolded 'we do' phase (Industry Jigsaw activity). However, the sequencing is not explicitly stated.

D2.evidence: The lesson plan includes some scaffolds (Use-Case Canvas) but lacks explicit plans to fade supports and provoke self-explanation. The instructor support is limited to circulating and probing for metrics, risks, and governance.

D3.evidence: The lesson plan includes independent tasks (Industry Jigsaw activity) but lacks a clear circulation/monitoring plan with error interception. The assessment task also does not include monitoring or feedback.

E1.evidence: The lesson plan has a simple→complex progression (core components → Industry Jigsaw activity) but lacks explicit scaffolding and goal-free early tasks.

E2.evidence: The lesson plan includes some integrated materials (slides, one-page scenarios) but lacks concise on-screen text, narration aligned with visuals, and brief processing pauses. The instructor support is limited to circulating and probing for metrics, risks, and governance.

E3.evidence: The lesson plan includes some early probe (mini-poll prompts) but lacks explicit supports fading and quick effort/load checks. The instructor support is limited to circulating and probing for metrics, risks, and governance.

F1.evidence: The lesson plan includes multiple means of representation/action/engagement (slides, one-page scenarios, Use-Case Canvas) but lacks clear instructions and proactive accommodations. The instructor support is limited to circulating and probing for metrics, risks, and governance.

F2.evidence: The lesson plan includes some error-friendly norms (instructor support, circulation) but lacks structured reflection linked to ILOs. The assessment task also does not include progress tracking or reflection.
